Replay

View pool foundations

5 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Optional property cachingIdentity and ownershipTyped entity bindingsDetached projection and samplingAnimation without repainting data

Use view pools to give live entities Godot scenes and retire those scenes when the entity identity ends. Nodes2 manages scene instances by key; typed pools add entity generation handles, detached display values and callback bindings. The Godot bridge goal describes that layering.

Nodes2 uses bounded indexed identity lookup, with a separate preflight index for each presentation batch. Zero and duplicate keys are rejected before changing scene instances. Retained keys retain their node; absent identities retire before new ones allocate, so a full pool can replace every identity in one call. The map preserves lowest-vacant-slot allocation and performs no per-frame Odin allocation. A fully retained membership batch skips capacity scans and index/free-slot rebuilds after complete preflight. Sparse indexes clear only recorded occupied buckets; each index adds four bytes per configured entry for those bucket locations. Scene creation/free still occurs when identities enter/leave.

Capacity is 1–65536. Each index uses a power-of-two table with at most half its buckets occupied. Lookup is expected constant time, with a bounded full-table probe limit; it is not a worst-case constant-time hash guarantee. The extra index, free-slot and cached-value arrays increase presentation-owner memory in exchange for fewer repeated scans. They do not enter World, history or network packets.

Optional property caching#

Existing callers keep cache_properties=false, so every call reapplies position, rotation, scale and modulation as before. An adapter that exclusively owns those four root properties can opt in:

Odin
views.cache_properties = true
ok := scenegd.nodes_present(&views, instances)

The first presentation applies all properties. Later calls apply only changed values. The cache compares desired values, not Godot state, so it does not need four engine reads per node. If animation/editor/game code changes an owned property, invalidate before the next presentation:

Odin
scenegd.nodes_invalidate(&views, entity_key) // one view
scenegd.nodes_invalidate(&views)             // all views

Invalidation does not respawn the view or restart effects. Turning caching off reapplies all values. Keep independently animated children separate from root properties controlled by this binding, or explicitly invalidate after an external write. Callers still own any game-specific child state and cleanup policy.

Nodes2.stats counts scene creations/retirements and property writes/skips. The two indexes count probes. These are local diagnostics, not simulation state.

Identity and ownership#

view.handle_key(handle) encodes the complete nonzero pool generation and index. Use a separate view pool for each source pool/timeline scope; the key does not globally identify a pool. An invalid handle returns zero. A replacement generation gets a new view. Clear views at an explicit session/epoch boundary when identities can otherwise repeat. The typed owner below handles scope changes automatically.

The parent must outlive Nodes2. It owns the scene reference and its child views; external code may borrow a node from nodes_get but must not free it behind the owner. nodes_destroy releases references and queues node retirement. Engine retirement completes asynchronously. Failure to instantiate a scene is explicit; the existing API does not promise rollback of earlier scene lifecycle operations in that call.

Pure index tests cover duplicates, collisions, capacity, reset and handle lifetime. tests/replay_nodes/run.sh exercises actual Godot properties, retained/replaced instances, opt-in behavior, external-write invalidation and resource retirement. The benchmark compares the preserved old owner, indexed owner and cached owner with the same scene/input workload. Timings isolate presentation calls, not GPU rendering or total game performance.

Typed entity bindings#

View_Pool2(Entity, Value, Rig) owns one source entity pool's views. Value is a pointer-free presentation value; Rig caches child nodes and may own local resources. The parent and callback user must outlive the owner. attach returns a rig once per new view; paint runs initially and when Value changes; detach releases rig resources before the node retires. A failed attach also receives detach, so cleanup must accept a partially initialized rig. Callbacks must not reenter this owner.

Odin
Actor_UI :: struct { health: i32 }
Actor_Rig :: struct { label: gd.Label }
views: scenegd.View_Pool2(Actor, Actor_UI, Actor_Rig)
binding := scenegd.View_Binding(Actor_UI, Actor_Rig){
    attach = proc(_: rawptr, node: gd.Node2d) -> (Actor_Rig, bool) {
        label := cast(gd.Label)gd.get_node(node, "Health")
        return {label}, label != nil
    },
    paint = proc(_: rawptr, rig: ^Actor_Rig, ui: Actor_UI) {
        gd.set_text(rig.label, fmt.ctprintf("%d", ui.health))
    },
}
ok := scenegd.view_pool_load(&views, parent, "res://actor.tscn", 128, binding)
// items contain typed handles and detached Entity_View(Actor_UI) values.
error := scenegd.view_pool_present(&views, {epoch, view_revision}, items)
// When leaving: scenegd.view_pool_destroy(&views).

The typed owner caches root position/rotation/scale/color automatically. Reserve those properties for this owner. view_pool_invalidate(&views, handle) invalidates both root properties and typed paint; omitting the handle invalidates all views. Do not mutate or free borrowed nodes outside these ownership rules. A changed scope recreates every rig, even when numeric handles repeat. Older epochs are rejected; revision is a caller-supplied reset token, not an authority credential. Generations distinguish reused entity slots within one scope.

Invalid values, duplicates and capacity are preflighted before scene changes. Instantiation/attachment can fail after lifecycle work starts; that failure clears the typed owner and is explicit. It does not restore old scene nodes. Payload comparison uses value equality, not padding bytes. Floating values that differ continually will repaint; choose a quantized UI value when appropriate.

Detached projection and sampling#

replay.project(&timeline, tick, proc(World)->Display) selects a retained frame and returns a pointer-free value. The callback receives World by value and cannot mutate history through a borrowed pointer; timeline mutation reentry is refused. It does not promise zero copying or automatically shrink the result. Keep Display small when reducing copy costs matters. Hello demonstrates a full view batch for clarity; its small World is actually smaller than that batch.

view.project_pool fills a reusable bounded Projection(Entity, Value) from a detached pool. Its typed entity callback returns (Entity_View(Value), include); false filters a member. Invalid/capacity failures preserve the previous output. Projection owners allocate at initialization and allocate nothing per call.

projection_select requires explicit predicted, observed or authoritative input. Local_Predicted_Remote_Observed takes local-owner entities from prediction and others from observation, preserving each item's source and tick. Missing sources, mismatched scopes, and conflicting lifetimes/ownership in one slot are errors. Selection never grants simulation authority. Feed sources from the corresponding runner APIs; labeling a value does not establish its provenance.

projection_blend interpolates poses only for matching handles and teleport cut values. Before alpha reaches one, membership and discrete UI come from the older sample. Changed cuts snap the pose; changed scopes choose the newer batch directly. It refuses mixed-source interpolation and backward tick pairs. For mixed displays, interpolate observation first, then select local prediction. Keep destination and source owners distinct. Projection storage is presentation-owned and must not be mutated while another operation consumes it.

See the compile-checked Hello and tests/replay_nodes examples, and typed bridge evidence.

Animation without repainting data#

An optional View_Binding.frame(user, rig, value, dt) hook advances presentation animation even when the detached Value is unchanged and paint is skipped. Call view_pool_frame(&views, dt) once after presenting a successful batch. It visits live entries only and rejects negative/nonfinite delta without callbacks. The callback receives the retained detached value and may animate rig-owned children; root pose/scale/modulation remain owned by the pool. Callbacks must not reenter or change pool membership. Simulation time and presentation time remain separate.

Scrapyard's enemy bridge uses paint for texture/telegraph/health changes and frame for idle/attack/death animation, status flicker and hit wobble. A cached unchanged value therefore does not freeze an idle animation. This hook is optional for existing bindings; no frame callback is invoked by view_pool_present itself.
